Constraints stated during conversation:
- [ACTIVE] No clear path to staff at current company (explicit feedback, structural)

- [ACTIVE] 80% base salary cut for Option B, 0.8% equity
- [ACTIVE] Family: wife physician (primary earner), two kids (7,4)
- [ACTIVE] Financially survivable for Option B (mortgage fine, modest cuts)

step6_output.answer_core:
Don't treat this as a static choice among three labels. You have a sequencing problem, not a comparison problem.

First, buy time. Ask all three companies for a deadline extension—48 to 72 hours is usually obtainable and changes nothing for them while giving you room to run the real decision gates.

Gate 1: The conversation with your wife. This is not a courtesy; it is a hard unlock condition for Option B. You need explicit joint buy-in on what an 80% base cut means for household risk psychology, not just spreadsheet survivability. If she is not fully in, Option B is off the table. Full stop.

If Gate 1 clears, open Gate 2: due diligence and negotiation on the Series B. Do not accept the offer as presented. Negotiate a six-month compensation ramp (e.g., 50% cut month 1-3, 65% month 4-6, full reduced base month 7+), remote/hybrid boundaries, and explicit role scope/title protections. Run evidence checks on runway (18+ months?), CEO hiring/firing track record, equity terms (0.8% on what base? 4-year vest? acceleration on change of control?), and likely dilution through Series C. If any of these come back weak, Option B is off the table.

If Option B fails at either gate, take Option A. Frame it explicitly as a 24-month bridge, not a solution to your desire to build. Set a calendar reminder for month 18 to start evaluating founding or early-stage opportunities again, so this does not become another passive drift.

Option C—staying—is not a safe default. It is an active choice to accept structural decline. Given the explicit feedback that there is no staff path, staying should only be a fallback if both A and B fall through, and even then you should set a hard 12-month exit timeline.
